fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. Amos 3:1 says the LORD's word is against the whole family He brought up out of the land of Egypt. He is speaking to the children of Israel. Nice pick.
Assyria is a real place in the Bible, but it's not the one in this verse. Amos 3:1 says the family was brought up out of the land of Egypt. Egypt is the one to remember here.
Babylon is a good Bible name, so I see why it came to mind. But this verse says the whole family was brought up out of the land of Egypt. Hold onto Egypt for this one, friend.

Yes, baker! The question is, “Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey?” The answer is built right in: a lion roars when he has prey. Amos asks it again about a young lion: “Does a young lion growl in his den if he has caught nothing?”
Storms are a fine guess, but they're not in this verse. Amos 3:4 asks if a lion roars in the forest when he has no prey. So the roar goes with prey, not weather.

Traps can be sneaky, so I see where you're coming from. But Amos 3:5 asks, “Does a trap spring from the ground when it has nothing to catch?” The word is catch, not hide. The question is about the trap having something to catch.
Tremble, baker! Amos asks, “If a ram’s horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble?” When the horn sounds in a city, the people tremble. The answer is built right into the question.
I like the optimism, friend. But the verse asks, “If a ram’s horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble?” The people tremble, not rejoice. Keep that hopeful spirit for another verse.

Right! The text says, “Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan to His servants the prophets.” Just after that, the passage says, “The Lord GOD has spoken—who will not prophesy?” (Amos 3:8). So the prophets are the ones He shares His plan with.
That's it, baker! They're told to see the great unrest in the city and the acts of oppression in her midst. Ashdod and Egypt are called to take a look. I think this one hurts.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, “They store up violence and destruction in their citadels.” A citadel is a stronghold, and what they've stored up in theirs is not good. I think this one hurts.
Jacob, baker! The Lord GOD, the God of Hosts, says, “Hear and testify against the house of Jacob…” That name is the one that fills the blank. Well done.

Egypt did show up earlier in the passage, so I get the pull. But this verse says, “the horns of the altar will be cut off, and they will fall to the ground.” The horns fall to the ground, not off to Egypt.
